defects.title: WC-4 contract path <output-dir>/return-contract.yaml breaks for file-valued, fixed or generated outputs
defects.quote: In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`).
defects.what_goes_wrong: For tdd and init-lite (and possibly spec-panel) the brief passes `--output <file>`, so WC-4 yields `<file>/return-contract.yaml` inside a regular file (verified: writing it fails 'Not a directory' and `test -s` exits 1), and for commands with fixed or run-generated locations (cleanup-audit `.claude-audit/`, index-repo, adversarial `<output>/adversarial/`, workflow `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/`, implement beside the ledger) there is no `--output` directory or the row names a different path, so the coordinator cannot know the contract path before dispatch and 7.2 step 3-4 / AC-1.2 / AC-2.2 / AC-2.3 cannot pass as written.
defects.is_fixed_when: The spec gives, for every command that writes a contract (every 3.1/3.2 row), one contract path that is a valid file path derivable before dispatch (or explicitly states the exception and how the worker/coordinator learns it), with explicit rules for file-valued `--output` (tdd, init-lite, spec-panel) and fixed/generated locations (cleanup-audit, index-repo, adversarial, workflow, implement, pr-submit), and WC-4, section 2.3, the 3.x rows and 7.2 steps 3-4 all agree on it.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting WC-4's fixed path or dropping tdd/init-lite from the worker set removes the known-before-dispatch report requirement that 7.2 and WC-5 depend on; only a consistent per-command path rule fixes it (narrowing scope with matching AC changes would be acceptable only if every remaining command gets a valid path).
defects.present_in_others_hint: Section 2.3 brief text (line 73), the 'Contract' definition at line 76, rows for adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, init-lite, tdd, workflow, spec-panel, implement, pr-submit, research; 7.2 steps 3-4 and 6; AC-1.2, AC-1.4, AC-2.2, AC-2.3.

defects.title: Revised spec gives init-lite/cleanup-audit/index-repo contracts but denies them the unattended section
defects.quote: run d4-r2 (arm ab4), file p16/ab4/runs/d4-r2/aud/ws/.dev/orca-command-refactor/specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:76: "Every command whose row names an unattended-mode change in P1-P3 also gains the `## Unattended mode` section (section 2.1); brainstorm and init-lite (no change)"
defects.what_goes_wrong: In the d4-r2 revised spec WC-4 (line 62) names contract paths for init-lite, cleanup-audit and index-repo, while line 76 says init-lite gains no section (so no `--unattended`, no contract, and line 79's 'until Phase 1 adds the contract' never ends for it) and AC-1.1/AC-1.2 (lines 195-196) sweep in the P1-labelled adversarial/cleanup-audit/index-repo rows whose 'small fix' wording names no unattended-mode change, so an implementer following one text fails the other and a successful init-lite worker is reported failed under WC-5.
defects.is_fixed_when: One rule states which ready commands gain `--unattended`, the `## Unattended mode` section and a contract, and WC-4's path list, the section-3 intro, the 3.1 rows (init-lite, cleanup-audit, index-repo, adversarial), the P1 scope and AC-1.1/AC-1.2 all name the same set.
defects.deletion_note: Yes in part: removing init-lite (and any command without the section) from WC-4's path list and narrowing AC-1.1/AC-1.2 consistently is a valid fix, as long as the worker report rule for those commands (named file, WC-5 outcome) is stated.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Revised WC-4 (line 62), section 2.3 (line 73), section 3 intro (76), 3.1 intro (79), rows 83/85-87, P1 scope (159), AC-1.1/AC-1.2 (195-196), WC-5 'no report exists'.

extra_noticed.title: 'Every changed command' gains the section, but AC-1.1 requires it on all 3.1-3.2 commands
extra_noticed.quote: Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section (section 2.1).
extra_noticed.what_goes_wrong: Brainstorm and init-lite have small fix 'None' so an implementer following line 76 gives them no section, yet AC-1.1 asserts every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has one (and P1 makes every 3.1/3.2 command accept `--unattended`), so AC-1.1 fails.
extra_noticed.is_fixed_when: Line 76, the P1 scope and AC-1.1 name the same set of commands that gain the `## Unattended mode` section.
extra_noticed.deletion_note: Yes: narrowing AC-1.1 to the changed commands, or widening line 76 to all 3.1-3.2 commands, each fixes it if applied consistently.
